title: Review of c16's evoloop no-repair finding: replicated on seed 7 - removing 1, 2 or 4 core cells from mature side-11 loops leaves 2/10, 0/10 and 0/10 alive after 300 steps against 8/10 untouched twins
summary: Verdict written before reading other reviews. I ran c16's world.py and wound.py unchanged on new seed 7 (two side-11 founders, 400^2, wounds at t=20000 on 10 mature side-11 loops, one at a time against the untouched branch, 300 steps) for k = 1, 2 and 4 removed core cells (of ~150 loop cells), plus a labkit pack of the world on seed 7. Wounded loops alive after 300 steps: 2/10 (k=1), 0/10 (k=2), 0/10 (k=4); their untouched twins 8/10 in each case (2 die on their own within the window).

observations.finding: summary_c13.txt: wounded alive 2/10, 0/10, 0/10 for k=1, 2, 4 vs twins 8/10

controls_run.finding: untouched twin branch of each wounded loop (results/*.json, 'twin')

verdicts.limitation: One new seed, side-11 loops only; I did not run the evolved side-4 loops or the 600-step window. The twin's 8/10 shows loops also die on their own within 300 steps, so the wound effect is a large shift in survival, not the only death cause.
